components.note: ⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — counting rods were bamboo; also in 笑 smile, 筷 chopsticks.
寿 (shòu) is only a loose sound clue for chóu.
石 (stone) — stones and minerals: 破, 研, 砖; 码 first meant stone weights, then numbers.
马 (mǎ) sounds exactly like 码; also in 吗, 骂 mà, 妈 mā.

example.hanzi: 他把手里的筹码全部推到了桌子中间。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ shǒu lǐ de chóumǎ quánbù tuī dào le zhuōzi zhōngjiān.
example.english: He pushed all the chips in his hand to the middle of the table.
example.fact: Casino poker chips are deliberately made heavier than they look — often around 8 to 10 grams each, made from compression-molded clay composites — partly so they feel satisfying to stack and shuffle, and partly to make counterfeiting with cheap plastic harder to disguise.

examples.hanzi: 谈判时，我们手里的筹码不多。
examples.pinyin: Tánpàn shí, wǒmen shǒu lǐ de chóumǎ bù duō.
examples.english: We don't have many bargaining chips in the negotiation.

examples.hanzi: 赌场里的筹码可以换成现金。
examples.pinyin: Dǔchǎng lǐ de chóumǎ kěyǐ huànchéng xiànjīn.
examples.english: Casino chips can be exchanged for cash.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
辶 (walk) — movement and distance, as in 过, 近, 进: 远 is a road that goes far.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuǎn; 元 also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.

example.hanzi: 我老远就看见你在路口等我了。
example.pinyin: wǒ lǎoyuǎn jiù kànjiàn nǐ zài lùkǒu děng wǒ le.
example.english: I saw you waiting at the intersection from very far away.
example.fact: The curvature of the Earth limits how far an object can be seen from ground level on a clear day — a person 1.7 meters tall can typically see the horizon only about 4.7 kilometers away, which is why lighthouses and watchtowers were built as tall as possible, to extend the distance ships could be spotted.

examples.hanzi: 他老远跑来看我，我很感动。
examples.pinyin: Tā lǎoyuǎn pǎo lái kàn wǒ, wǒ hěn gǎndòng.
examples.english: He came all that way to see me, and I was touched.

examples.hanzi: 声音从老远的地方传过来。
examples.pinyin: Shēngyīn cóng lǎoyuǎn de dìfang chuán guòlái.
examples.english: The sound came from far away.

meanings: to pass on to sb else

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — passing things along, as in 道 road, 送 send, 过 pass.
弟 (dì) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 第 dì and 梯 tī.

example.hanzi: 志愿者们把火炬一站一站地传递下去。
example.pinyin: zhìyuànzhě men bǎ huǒjù yī zhàn yī zhàn de chuándì xiàqù.
example.english: The volunteers passed the torch along, one relay station at a time.
example.fact: The modern Olympic torch relay was invented for the 1936 Berlin Games, not ancient Greece — it was devised by German organizing official Carl Diem as a piece of political theater, and the practice of relaying a flame across countries before the opening ceremony has continued at every Games since.

examples.hanzi: 请把这份文件传递给下一位同事。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè fèn wénjiàn chuándì gěi xià yī wèi tóngshì.
examples.english: Please pass this document on to the next colleague.

examples.hanzi: 眼神也能传递很多信息。
examples.pinyin: Yǎnshén yě néng chuándì hěn duō xìnxī.
examples.english: Eye contact can also convey a lot of information.

components.note: 酋 (wine jar) with a hand 寸 offering it: honoring a guest. 尊 sounds out 遵 zūn (obey) and 樽 zūn (goblet).

example.hanzi: 我们要尊重老人。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zūnzhòng lǎorén.
example.english: We should respect older people.
example.fact: 尊 gives 尊敬 (respect people, admiration) and 尊重 (respect opinions, rights). It is also the measure word for statues and cannons (一尊佛像), and appears in 尊称 (honorific).

examples.hanzi: 学生们都很尊敬老师。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshengmen dōu hěn zūnjìng lǎoshī.
examples.english: The students all respect their teacher.

examples.hanzi: 请问您尊姓大名？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn nín zūnxìng dàmíng?
examples.english: May I ask your honorable name?

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — hand actions; 拖 is to drag, as in 拉 pull, 推 push.
廴 (long stride) — stretching a journey out; also in 建 build. 延 also sounds out 诞 dàn.

example.hanzi: 他总是拖延交作业的时间，结果每次都很紧张。
example.pinyin: tā zǒngshì tuōyán jiāo zuòyè de shíjiān, jiéguǒ měicì dōu hěn jǐnzhāng.
example.english: He always delays turning in his homework, so it's always stressful in the end.
example.fact: The word 'procrastination' comes from Latin 'procrastinare,' meaning 'to put off until tomorrow,' and the Roman statesman Cicero used the word as an insult against a political rival — a reminder that complaints about chronic delay are at least two thousand years old.

examples.hanzi: 别再拖延了，今天就把事情做完吧。
examples.pinyin: Bié zài tuōyán le, jīntiān jiù bǎ shìqing zuò wán ba.
examples.english: Stop procrastinating and finish the job today.

examples.hanzi: 会议因为下雨被拖延了半个小时。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì yīnwèi xiàyǔ bèi tuōyán le bàn gè xiǎoshí.
examples.english: The meeting was delayed by half an hour because of the rain.

components.note: 彳 (step, walk) — the road family: 行 go, 往 toward. 徽 originally meant a cord; the 'emblem, badge' sense is a later extension (徽章).
糸 (silk thread; here 系) — the old meaning is a rope. 徽 looks like 微 (wēi) with a thread added; the sound link to huī is only loose.
音 (sound) — 音 over 十 — a full piece of music, so a section; 章 sounds out 彰 zhāng and 障 zhàng.

example.hanzi: 她把童子军徽章一枚一枚地缝在制服上。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ tóngzǐjūn huīzhāng yī méi yī méi de féng zài zhìfú shàng.
example.english: She sewed the scout badges onto her uniform one by one.
example.fact: The Boy Scouts of America currently offers over 135 different merit badges, ranging from Astronomy to Welding, and a scout must earn 21 specific ones — including mandatory badges like First Aid and Citizenship — to reach the rank of Eagle Scout.

examples.hanzi: 他的外套上别着一枚红色的徽章。
examples.pinyin: Tā de wàitào shàng bié zhe yī méi hóngsè de huīzhāng.
examples.english: He has a red badge pinned to his coat.

examples.hanzi: 每所大学都有自己的徽章。
examples.pinyin: Měi suǒ dàxué dōu yǒu zìjǐ de huīzhāng.
examples.english: Every university has its own emblem.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骑 ride, 驾; 骗 first meant to jump on a horse.
扁 (biǎn) — near sound — 骗 is piàn; 扁 also sounds out 偏 piān, 篇 piān and 遍 biàn.
尺 (ruler) — the main part, as in 尺寸 size. Dictionary story: a place where measures are discussed (口), like a bureau; 局 also means 'game' as in 结局.
口 (mouth/box) — placed inside 尺. It represents talk or a space; Memory aid: a ruler fitted to a mouth means rules are discussed in an 'office'.

example.hanzi: 警方揭露了一起涉及数百万元的投资骗局。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng jiēlù le yī qǐ shèjí shùbǎiwàn yuán de tóuzī piànjú.
example.english: Police exposed an investment scam involving millions of yuan.
example.fact: The Ponzi scheme is named after Charles Ponzi, who in 1920 promised investors 50 percent returns in 45 days by supposedly arbitraging international postal reply coupons; he took in roughly $15 million (well over $200 million today) before the scheme collapsed within about a year.

examples.hanzi: 这显然是一个骗局，千万别上当。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiǎnrán shì yī gè piànjú, qiānwàn bié shàngdàng.
examples.english: This is clearly a scam. Don't fall for it.

examples.hanzi: 老人差点被电话里的骗局骗走了存款。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén chàdiǎn bèi diànhuà lǐ de piànjú piànzǒu le cúnkuǎn.
examples.english: The old man almost lost his savings to a phone scam.

components.note: 人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
彳 (step, walk) — 彳 is the left-step radical, as in 行, 径, 德; 往 is going toward.
王 (wáng) — near sound — 往 is wǎng, same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 以往我们从没遇到过这么严重的问题。
example.pinyin: yǐwǎng wǒmen cóng méi yùdào guò zhème yánzhòng de wèntí.
example.english: In the past we never encountered such a serious problem.
example.fact: Ice cores drilled from Antarctica preserve tiny bubbles of ancient air, letting scientists directly measure atmospheric CO2 levels from as far back as 800,000 years in the past — records that show today's carbon dioxide concentration is higher than at any point in that entire span.

examples.hanzi: 以往这个时候，街上人很多。
examples.pinyin: Yǐwǎng zhège shíhou, jiē shàng rén hěn duō.
examples.english: In the past, the streets were crowded at this time.

examples.hanzi: 今年的成绩比以往任何一年都好。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de chéngjì bǐ yǐwǎng rènhé yī nián dōu hǎo.
examples.english: This year's results are better than any previous year.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 优 first meant a person who performs or is excellent, in 演员 and 优秀.
尤 (yóu) — near sound — 优 is yōu; 尤 also sounds out 忧 yōu.
儿 (legs, person) — with a foot 𠂉 above: a foot stepping out in front of a person, so "first, earlier".

example.hanzi: 紧急病人应该优先接受治疗。
example.pinyin: jǐnjí bìngrén yīnggāi yōuxiān jiēshòu zhìliáo.
example.english: Emergency patients should receive treatment with priority.
example.fact: Hospital emergency rooms use a formal system called triage — from the French 'trier,' meaning 'to sort' — first developed on Napoleonic battlefields by French military surgeon Dominique Jean Larrey, who prioritized treating soldiers by the severity of their wounds rather than by rank.

examples.hanzi: 老人和孕妇可以优先上车。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén hé yùnfù kěyǐ yōuxiān shàngchē.
examples.english: Elderly people and pregnant women may board first.

examples.hanzi: 在这个公司，客户的需求永远优先。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhège gōngsī, kèhù de xūqiú yǒngyuǎn yōuxiān.
examples.english: At this company, customers' needs always come first.

components.note: 八 (eight) — originally two strokes pulling apart, meaning divide; that sense is in 分 divide, 公 public and 半 half.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 会议定在明天早上八点开始。
example.pinyin: huìyì dìng zài míngtiān zǎoshang bā diǎn kāishǐ.
example.english: The meeting is set to start at eight o'clock tomorrow morning.
example.fact: Mechanical clocks with hour hands only became common in Europe in the 14th century; before that, most people tracked time using sundials, water clocks, or church bells, and an 'hour' could vary in length depending on the season since daylight was divided into twelve equal parts regardless of how long the day actually was.

examples.hanzi: 我每天早上八点出门上班。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang bā diǎn chūmén shàngbān.
examples.english: I leave for work at eight every morning.

examples.hanzi: 电影八点开始，你别迟到了。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng bā diǎn kāishǐ, nǐ bié chídào le.
examples.english: The movie starts at eight, so don't be late.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国 country, 回 return, 图 map; 园 is a fenced garden.
元 (yuán) sounds exactly like 园; also in 远 yuǎn, 院 yuàn, 完 wán.

example.hanzi: 周末我们打算带孩子去动物园看熊猫。
example.pinyin: zhōumò wǒmen dǎsuàn dài háizi qù dòngwùyuán kàn xióngmāo.
example.english: This weekend we plan to take the kids to the zoo to see the pandas.
example.fact: The Vienna Zoo, founded in 1752 as part of the Habsburg imperial menagerie, is the oldest continuously operating zoo in the world — it began as a private collection of exotic animals for the Austrian royal family before opening to the public decades later.

examples.hanzi: 动物园里的大象特别受孩子们欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ de dàxiàng tèbié shòu háizimen huānyíng.
examples.english: The elephants at the zoo are especially popular with children.

examples.hanzi: 你去过北京动物园吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ qùguo Běijīng dòngwùyuán ma?
examples.english: Have you ever been to the Beijing Zoo?

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 稳定的收入能给人带来很大的安全感。
example.pinyin: wěndìng de shōurù néng gěi rén dàilái hěn dà de ānquángǎn.
example.english: A stable income can give a person a great sense of security.
example.fact: Psychologist Abraham Maslow placed safety and security needs directly above basic physiological needs like food and water in his 1943 hierarchy of needs, arguing that people cannot fully pursue higher goals like relationships or self-actualization until they feel reasonably secure in their environment.

examples.hanzi: 她觉得一个人走夜路没有安全感。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéde yī gè rén zǒu yèlù méiyǒu ānquángǎn.
examples.english: She feels unsafe walking alone at night.

examples.hanzi: 孩子需要父母给他足够的安全感。
examples.pinyin: Háizi xūyào fùmǔ gěi tā zúgòu de ānquángǎn.
examples.english: Children need their parents to give them enough of a sense of security.

components.note: 争 (contend) — simplified from 爭, two hands pulling at the same object. See 战争 war and 竞争 compete.
寸 (hand, also "inch") — a grasping hand seizing something; also in 对, 守, 寺.

example.hanzi: 两个国家为争夺这片油田爆发了冲突。
example.pinyin: liǎng gè guójiā wèi zhēngduó zhè piàn yóutián bàofā le chōngtū.
example.english: The two countries broke into conflict fighting over this oil field.
example.fact: The Spratly Islands in the South China Sea — a scattering of mostly uninhabitable reefs and rocks — are claimed in whole or in part by six different governments, largely because the surrounding waters are believed to sit atop significant untapped oil and natural gas reserves.

examples.hanzi: 两支球队正在争夺冠军。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng zhī qiúduì zhèngzài zhēngduó guànjūn.
examples.english: The two teams are fighting for the championship.

examples.hanzi: 兄弟俩为争夺遗产吵了起来。
examples.pinyin: Xiōngdì liǎ wèi zhēngduó yíchǎn chǎo le qǐlái.
examples.english: The two brothers argued over the inheritance.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 探 is to reach out and feel, then to explore.
The right half is a sound part shared with 深 shēn: a loose clue for tàn.
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: a steep place, a risky pass.
佥 (qiān) is a loose sound clue for xiǎn; 佥 also in 检 jiǎn, 剑 jiàn, 脸 liǎn and 验 yàn.

example.hanzi: 他花了三年时间在亚马逊雨林里探险。
example.pinyin: tā huā le sān nián shíjiān zài Yàmǎxùn yǔlín lǐ tànxiǎn.
example.english: He spent three years exploring the Amazon rainforest.
example.fact: The Amazon rainforest is so vast and dense that scientists estimate previously undocumented species are still being discovered there at a rate of roughly one every two days, including plants, fish, and amphibians never before catalogued.

examples.hanzi: 我们打算暑假去沙漠探险。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎsuàn shǔjià qù shāmò tànxiǎn.
examples.english: We plan to go exploring in the desert this summer.

examples.hanzi: 这本书讲的是一次危险的探险经历。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū jiǎng de shì yī cì wēixiǎn de tànxiǎn jīnglì.
examples.english: This book is about a dangerous expedition.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话; 辩 puts two 辛 (offenders) with words between them, an argument.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.
彳 (step) — walking and conduct, as in 行, 往, 得, 很.
聿 (brush) — writing the rules: 律 is law, and a rule of rhythm.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.hanzi: 被告的辩护律师在法庭上提出了新的证据。
example.pinyin: bèigào de biànhù lǜshī zài fǎtíng shàng tíchū le xīn de zhèngjù.
example.english: The defendant's defense lawyer presented new evidence in court.
example.fact: The right to a defense lawyer even for those who cannot afford one was only firmly established in the United States by the 1963 Supreme Court case Gideon v. Wainwright, after Clarence Earl Gideon, a man too poor to hire an attorney, successfully argued his own appeal from prison with a handwritten petition.

examples.hanzi: 他请了一位有经验的辩护律师。
examples.pinyin: Tā qǐng le yī wèi yǒu jīngyàn de biànhù lǜshī.
examples.english: He hired an experienced defense lawyer.

examples.hanzi: 辩护律师要求法庭重新调查这起案子。
examples.pinyin: Biànhù lǜshī yāoqiú fǎtíng chóngxīn diàochá zhè qǐ ànzi.
examples.english: The defense lawyer asked the court to reinvestigate the case.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — digging by hand; also in 打 hit, 拉 pull.
穴 (cave, hole) — digging makes a hole; as in 空 empty, 窗 window.
扌 (hand) — digging by hand; also in 挖 dig, 拉 pull.
屈 (qū) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 崛 jué and 窟 kū.

example.hanzi: 考古学家在这片沙漠里挖掘出了古代城市的遗迹。
example.pinyin: kǎogǔ xuéjiā zài zhè piàn shāmò lǐ wājué chū le gǔdài chéngshì de yíjì.
example.english: Archaeologists excavated the remains of an ancient city in this desert.
example.fact: The ancient city of Pompeii was buried and preserved almost intact by volcanic ash from Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD, and organized excavation didn't begin until the 1740s — the city sat frozen and hidden for nearly 1,700 years before workers started digging up its remarkably well-preserved streets, buildings, and plaster casts of victims.

examples.hanzi: 工人们正在路边挖掘一条水沟。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zhèngzài lùbiān wājué yī tiáo shuǐgōu.
examples.english: Workers are digging a ditch by the road.

examples.hanzi: 老师鼓励我们挖掘自己的潜力。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī gǔlì wǒmen wājué zìjǐ de qiánlì.
examples.english: The teacher encourages us to tap into our own potential.

components.note: 乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).
戈 (spear) — weapons and war, as in 战 war, 武 martial.
翏 (liù) is only a loose sound clue for lù.

example.hanzi: 这部纪录片记录了那场战争中的大规模杀戮。
example.pinyin: zhè bù jìlùpiàn jìlù le nà chǎng zhànzhēng zhōng de dàguīmó shālù.
example.english: This documentary records the large-scale massacre that occurred during that war.
example.fact: The passenger pigeon, once North America's most numerous bird with an estimated population in the billions, was driven to extinction within a few decades through unrestricted commercial hunting — the last known wild bird was shot in 1901, and the species went extinct entirely by 1914.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影里有太多杀戮的画面。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ yǒu tài duō shālù de huàmiàn.
examples.english: This movie has too many scenes of slaughter.

examples.hanzi: 人们都希望这场杀戮早点结束。
examples.pinyin: Rénmen dōu xīwàng zhè chǎng shālù zǎodiǎn jiéshù.
examples.english: Everyone hopes the killing will end soon.

components.note: 冫 (ice, 两点水) — marks cold and freezing, as in 冷 cold, 冰 ice, 决; 凑 is coming together; 冫 here is water, not ice.
奏 (zòu) — close sound: 凑 còu. 奏 also sounds out 揍 zòu.

example.hanzi: 大家凑钱买了一个蛋糕。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā còu qián mǎi le yí gè dàngāo.
example.english: Everyone chipped in to buy a cake.
example.fact: 凑 is handy in colloquial phrases: 凑钱 (chip in), 凑合 (make do), 凑热闹 (join in the fun) and 凑巧 (by coincidence).

examples.hanzi: 今天人多，我们凑在一起吃饭吧。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān rén duō, wǒmen còu zài yìqǐ chīfàn ba.
examples.english: There are many people today, so let's eat together.

examples.hanzi: 他凑到我耳边小声说了几句话。
examples.pinyin: Tā còu dào wǒ ěrbiān xiǎoshēng shuō le jǐ jù huà.
examples.english: He leaned close to my ear and whispered a few words.

meanings: (to pick) the lesser of two evils

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家, 室, 安; 宁 is peace and calm at home.
丁 (dīng) — near sound — 宁 is níng; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng and 厅 tīng.
口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.

example.hanzi: 他宁可饿着肚子，也不愿意向别人借钱。
example.pinyin: tā nìngkě è zhe dùzi, yě bù yuànyì xiàng biérén jiè qián.
example.english: He would rather go hungry than borrow money from others.
example.fact: During the Great Depression, many unemployed Americans would rather sell apples on street corners for a nickel each than accept government relief, a phenomenon vivid enough that 'apple sellers' became a recognizable symbol of Depression-era pride and desperation in photographs of the time.

examples.hanzi: 我宁可走路，也不想挤公交车。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ nìngkě zǒulù, yě bù xiǎng jǐ gōngjiāochē.
examples.english: I'd rather walk than squeeze onto the bus.

examples.hanzi: 她宁可少睡点觉，也要把作业做完。
examples.pinyin: Tā nìngkě shǎo shuì diǎn jiào, yě yào bǎ zuòyè zuò wán.
examples.english: She'd rather sleep less than leave her homework unfinished.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — strolling, as in 道 road, 过 pass, 进 enter.
肖 (xiào) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 消 xiāo and 销 xiāo.
辶 (walk) — a long journey; also in 远 far, 道 road.
䍃 (yáo) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 摇 yáo and 谣 yáo.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.hanzi: 这个逃犯已经逍遥法外二十多年了。
example.pinyin: zhège táofàn yǐjīng xiāoyáo fǎwài èrshí duō nián le.
example.english: This fugitive has already been at large, beyond the reach of the law, for over twenty years.
example.fact: D.B. Cooper, who hijacked a Boeing 727 in 1971 and parachuted out with $200,000 in ransom money, remains the only unsolved case of air piracy in American aviation history — despite one of the largest FBI manhunts ever conducted, no confirmed trace of him or most of the money has ever been found.

examples.hanzi: 不能让坏人逍遥法外。
examples.pinyin: Bù néng ràng huàirén xiāoyáo fǎwài.
examples.english: We can't let bad people get away with it.

examples.hanzi: 他犯了罪却一直逍遥法外，大家都很气愤。
examples.pinyin: Tā fàn le zuì què yīzhí xiāoyáo fǎwài, dàjiā dōu hěn qìfèn.
examples.english: He committed a crime yet remains at large, and everyone is angry.

components.note: 幺 (small/thread) — the dictionary radical, as in 么 and 幻. 乡 is simplified from 鄉 (village); the three strokes here look like a thread. Memory aid: a thread looping home to the village.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 爷爷奶奶一直住在乡下，很少来城里。
example.pinyin: yéye nǎinai yīzhí zhù zài xiāngxia, hěn shǎo lái chénglǐ.
example.english: Grandpa and grandma have always lived in the countryside and rarely come to the city.
example.fact: More than half of the world's population has lived in urban areas only since around 2007, according to United Nations data — for the vast majority of human history, the overwhelming majority of people lived in the countryside, working the land rather than in cities.

examples.hanzi: 我小时候在乡下长大。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎoshíhou zài xiāngxia zhǎngdà.
examples.english: I grew up in the countryside as a child.

examples.hanzi: 乡下的空气比城里新鲜多了。
examples.pinyin: Xiāngxia de kōngqì bǐ chéng lǐ xīnxiān duō le.
examples.english: The air in the countryside is much fresher than in the city.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 财, 买, 费; 赋 first meant a tax to raise soldiers.
武 (wǔ) — loose hint — 赋 is fù.
予 (yǔ) — to give; as a part it sounds out 预 yù, 野 yě and 序 xù.

example.hanzi: 法律赋予每个公民平等的权利。
example.pinyin: fǎlǜ fùyǔ měi gè gōngmín píngděng de quánlì.
example.english: The law bestows equal rights on every citizen.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved into a basalt stele around 1754 BC in ancient Babylon, is one of the earliest known written legal codes to formally bestow specific rights and obligations on different classes of citizens, with 282 laws covering everything from trade disputes to family matters.

examples.hanzi: 这份工作赋予了她很大的责任。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn gōngzuò fùyǔ le tā hěn dà de zérèn.
examples.english: This job has given her a great deal of responsibility.

examples.hanzi: 作者赋予这个角色新的意义。
examples.pinyin: Zuòzhě fùyǔ zhège juésè xīn de yìyì.
examples.english: The author gave this character a new meaning.

meanings: variant of 迴避|回避[hui2 bi4]

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 逃; 避 is stepping aside.
辟 (bì) — same sound — 避 is bì, like 辟; 辟 also sounds out 壁 bì and 臂 bì.

example.hanzi: 法官因为与被告是亲戚，主动回避了这个案子。
example.pinyin: fǎguān yīnwèi yǔ bèigào shì qīnqi, zhǔdòng huíbì le zhège ànzi.
example.english: The judge voluntarily recused himself from the case because he was related to the defendant.
example.fact: Judicial recusal — a judge stepping aside to avoid even the appearance of bias — has ancient roots; Roman law already held that 'no one should be a judge in his own cause' (nemo judex in causa sua), a principle still cited in courts worldwide today.

examples.hanzi: 他总是回避我的问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì huíbì wǒ de wèntí.
examples.english: He always avoids my questions.

examples.hanzi: 有些话题大家都想回避。
examples.pinyin: Yǒuxiē huàtí dàjiā dōu xiǎng huíbì.
examples.english: There are some topics everyone wants to steer clear of.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — a ring that encloses; also in 国 country, 围 surround.
卷 (juǎn) gives a close sound; 圈 also reads juàn or juān.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 他在艺术圈子里认识了不少有名的画家。
example.pinyin: tā zài yìshù quānzi lǐ rènshi le bùshǎo yǒumíng de huàjiā.
example.english: He got to know quite a few famous painters within artistic circles.
example.fact: Sociologist Robin Dunbar proposed in the 1990s that humans can maintain only about 150 stable social relationships at once — now known as 'Dunbar's number' — based on a correlation he found between primate brain size and typical social group size across many species.

examples.hanzi: 他的朋友圈子很小，只有几个同学。
examples.pinyin: Tā de péngyou quānzi hěn xiǎo, zhǐyǒu jǐ gè tóngxué.
examples.english: His circle of friends is small, just a few classmates.

examples.hanzi: 孩子在院子里绕着圈子跑。
examples.pinyin: Háizi zài yuànzi lǐ rào zhe quānzi pǎo.
examples.english: The child ran in circles around the yard.

components.note: 工 (work) — a carpenter's tool shape: work, craftsman. 工 is a sound series: 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 功 gōng, 空 kōng.
禾 (grain) — grain radical — 程 first meant to measure grain, hence standard, then course and journey; also in 种, 秋, 稿.
呈 (chéng) — same sound — 程 is chéng; 呈 also sounds out 逞 chěng.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.hanzi: 这座大桥是由一位年轻的工程师设计的。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò dàqiáo shì yóu yī wèi niánqīng de gōngchéngshī shèjì de.
example.english: This bridge was designed by a young engineer.
example.fact: The Brooklyn Bridge's chief engineer, Washington Roebling, was partially paralyzed by decompression sickness after inspecting the underwater caissons during construction, and had to direct the rest of the 1883 project by watching progress through a telescope from his apartment window while his wife, Emily Roebling, managed the site in person.

examples.hanzi: 我哥哥是一名软件工程师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge shì yī míng ruǎnjiàn gōngchéngshī.
examples.english: My older brother is a software engineer.

examples.hanzi: 这位工程师检查了所有的机器。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi gōngchéngshī jiǎnchá le suǒyǒu de jīqì.
examples.english: The engineer inspected all the machines.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — 弓 as in 张, 弯, 弹 — characters of stretching and drawing; 强 is about strength like a strong bow.
皿 (dish) — 皿 is a vessel, as in 盘, 盒; 盗 is coveting what is not yours.
次 (drool) — 次 here originally pictured drooling — wanting something greedily.

example.hanzi: 从前这条山路上经常出现强盗打劫过路的商人。
example.pinyin: cóngqián zhè tiáo shānlù shàng jīngcháng chūxiàn qiángdào dǎjié guòlù de shāngrén.
example.english: In the past, bandits often appeared on this mountain road to rob passing merchants.
example.fact: The legendary outlaw Robin Hood, said to have robbed from the rich to give to the poor in medieval Sherwood Forest, may be based on several real outlaws recorded in English court documents from the 13th century, though no single confirmed historical figure matches the legend exactly.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的强盗抢走了银行的钱。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de qiángdào qiǎngzǒu le yínháng de qián.
examples.english: The robbers in the movie stole money from the bank.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事讲的是一群强盗的传说。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi jiǎng de shì yī qún qiángdào de chuánshuō.
examples.english: This story is a legend about a band of bandits.

meanings: erhua variant of 一塊|一块[yi1 kuai4]

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
土 (earth) — a lump of earth; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
夬 (guài) is a loose clue; 快 kuài shares it and sounds exactly like 块.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.hanzi: 周末我们一块儿去爬山吧。
example.pinyin: zhōumò wǒmen yīkuàir qù páshān ba.
example.english: Let's go hiking together this weekend.
example.fact: Mountaineers on Mount Everest are required by Nepalese regulation to climb with a certified guide, largely a response to the growing number of solo attempts; even so, more than 300 people have died on the mountain since record-keeping began, many while climbing in groups roped together for safety.

examples.hanzi: 你和我一块儿去吧，路上有个伴。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ hé wǒ yīkuàir qù ba, lùshang yǒu gè bàn.
examples.english: Come along with me, so we have company on the way.

examples.hanzi: 他们一块儿吃饭，一块儿回家。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yīkuàir chīfàn, yīkuàir huíjiā.
examples.english: They eat together and go home together.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — cutting cloth to make clothes; also as 衤 in 衬, 被.
戈 (spear) — the cutting blade; also in 战 war, 或 or.
冫 (ice) — here the ice form of 氵 (water): 决 first meant to break a dam, so a decisive break.
夬 (guài) is a loose sound clue for jué; 夬 also sounds out 快 kuài and 块 kuài.

example.hanzi: 最高法院对这起案件做出了最终裁决。
example.pinyin: zuìgāo fǎyuàn duì zhè qǐ ànjiàn zuò chū le zuìzhōng cáijué.
example.english: The Supreme Court made its final ruling on this case.
example.fact: The U.S. Supreme Court hears oral arguments in only about 60 to 70 cases per year out of roughly 7,000 to 8,000 petitions filed, meaning the overwhelming majority of requests for a ruling are simply denied without any written opinion at all.

examples.hanzi: 法院的裁决让双方都很意外。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn de cáijué ràng shuāngfāng dōu hěn yìwài.
examples.english: The court's ruling surprised both sides.

examples.hanzi: 裁判对这次犯规做出了公正的裁决。
examples.pinyin: Cáipàn duì zhè cì fànguī zuòchū le gōngzhèng de cáijué.
examples.english: The referee made a fair ruling on this foul.

components.note: 火 (fire) — marks burning and heat, as in 烧 burn, 灯 lamp, 热; 燃 is to burn.
然 (rán) gives the sound exactly: 燃 rán; 然 itself first meant burning, now it means 'so'.
斗 (dipper, measure) — measuring grain and liquids: 科, 斜, 升; 料 is rice 米 measured out, then material.

example.hanzi: 火箭发射需要消耗大量的燃料。
example.pinyin: huǒjiàn fāshè xūyào xiāohào dàliàng de ránliào.
example.english: Launching a rocket requires consuming a huge amount of fuel.
example.fact: The Saturn V rocket that carried Apollo astronauts to the moon burned through roughly 20 tons of fuel and oxidizer per second during liftoff, generating 7.5 million pounds of thrust — most of its total launch weight of 2.8 million kilograms was fuel alone.

examples.hanzi: 汽车快没燃料了，我们先去加油站吧。
examples.pinyin: Qìchē kuài méi ránliào le, wǒmen xiān qù jiāyóuzhàn ba.
examples.english: The car is almost out of fuel, so let's go to the gas station first.

examples.hanzi: 太阳能是一种不需要燃料的能源。
examples.pinyin: Tàiyángnéng shì yī zhǒng bù xūyào ránliào de néngyuán.
examples.english: Solar power is an energy source that needs no fuel.

components.note: 爫 (hand, claw) — a hand pressing down; the traditional account is a hand calming a woman, so 'settled, secure'. Treat as a memory aid.
女 (woman) — a family also in 好 good, 妈 mum, 姓 surname; here the person being settled. Used in 妥当 proper, 妥协 compromise.
十 (ten, many) — traditional 協 pairs 十 with three 力 (strength) side by side: many forces joined in effort, so cooperation.

example.hanzi: 双方经过长时间谈判，最终达成了妥协。
example.pinyin: shuāngfāng jīngguò cháng shíjiān tánpàn, zuìzhōng dáchéng le tuǒxié.
example.english: After lengthy negotiations, both sides finally reached a compromise.
example.fact: The Great Compromise of 1787, struck during the U.S. Constitutional Convention, resolved a deadlock between large and small states by creating a two-chamber Congress — a House of Representatives based on population and a Senate with equal representation per state — a structural compromise that still shapes American government today.

examples.hanzi: 在这件事上，我不会妥协。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhè jiàn shì shàng, wǒ bù huì tuǒxié.
examples.english: I won't compromise on this matter.

examples.hanzi: 夫妻之间有时需要互相妥协。
examples.pinyin: Fūqī zhījiān yǒushí xūyào hùxiāng tuǒxié.
examples.english: Couples sometimes need to compromise with each other.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
阝 (mound, 左耳旁 on the left) — land and hills, as in 院, 阳, 队. The right part is a simplification with no sound clue.

example.hanzi: 澳大利亚是世界上最小的大陆。
example.pinyin: Àodàlìyà shì shìjiè shàng zuì xiǎo de dàlù.
example.english: Australia is the smallest continent in the world.
example.fact: Geologists have identified a largely submerged eighth continent called Zealandia, about 94 percent of which lies underwater in the South Pacific — only New Zealand and a few small islands rise above the surface, though the landmass meets all the geological criteria of a continent.

examples.hanzi: 欧洲大陆的天气最近很冷。
examples.pinyin: Ōuzhōu dàlù de tiānqì zuìjìn hěn lěng.
examples.english: The weather on the European continent has been cold lately.

examples.hanzi: 很多台湾人经常去大陆旅游。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō Táiwān rén jīngcháng qù dàlù lǚyóu.
examples.english: Many Taiwanese often travel to the mainland.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
首 (head, first) — a picture of a head with hair on top, which became the word for first and chief: 首先, 元首, also a measure for songs.

example.hanzi: 犯罪嫌疑人最终选择向警方自首。
example.pinyin: fànzuì xiányírén zuìzhōng xuǎnzé xiàng jǐngfāng zìshǒu.
example.english: The criminal suspect ultimately chose to turn himself in to the police.
example.fact: Many legal systems, including China's and several U.S. states, offer reduced sentences for voluntary surrender before arrest, based on the idea that turning oneself in reflects genuine remorse and saves the state the cost and uncertainty of a manhunt.

examples.hanzi: 他后悔了，决定主动去警察局自首。
examples.pinyin: Tā hòuhuǐ le, juédìng zhǔdòng qù jǐngchájú zìshǒu.
examples.english: He regretted it and decided to turn himself in at the police station.

examples.hanzi: 主动自首的人通常会得到从轻处理。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔdòng zìshǒu de rén tōngcháng huì dédào cóngqīng chǔlǐ.
examples.english: People who turn themselves in voluntarily usually receive a lighter sentence.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; 草 is grass itself, as in 花 flower, 菜 vegetable.
早 (zǎo) shares the rhyme -ǎo with cǎo, a loose sound clue.
艹 (grass) — plants; 莓 is a berry plant, as in 草 grass, 花 flower.
每 (měi) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.

example.hanzi: 这个季节的草莓又大又甜。
example.pinyin: zhège jìjié de cǎoméi yòu dà yòu tián.
example.english: The strawberries this season are big and sweet.
example.fact: Botanically speaking, the strawberry isn't a true berry at all — its seeds sit on the outside rather than the inside, and each tiny yellow speck on the surface is actually a separate fruit in its own right, technically making the red flesh an 'accessory fruit.'

examples.hanzi: 我想买一盒草莓做蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī hé cǎoméi zuò dàngāo.
examples.english: I want to buy a box of strawberries to make a cake.

examples.hanzi: 妹妹最喜欢草莓味的冰淇淋。
examples.pinyin: Mèimei zuì xǐhuan cǎoméi wèi de bīngqílín.
examples.english: My younger sister loves strawberry ice cream the most.

components.note: 言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters: a warning is spoken.
敬 (jìng, respect) is a close sound clue for jǐng.
忄 (heart) — alertness of the heart; also in 怕 afraid, 快 happy.
易 (yì) is a loose clue; 踢 tī shares it and sounds like 惕 tì.

example.hanzi: 面对陌生人的电话，大家应该保持警惕。
example.pinyin: miànduì mòshēngrén de diànhuà, dàjiā yīnggāi bǎochí jǐngtì.
example.english: Everyone should stay vigilant when receiving calls from strangers.
example.fact: Air traffic controllers are required to take mandatory breaks roughly every two hours because sustained, high-stakes vigilance sharply degrades after that point — a well-documented cognitive effect first studied systematically by psychologist Norman Mackworth during World War II radar operator research.

examples.hanzi: 你要警惕那些陌生人发来的链接。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào jǐngtì nàxiē mòshēngrén fā lái de liànjiē.
examples.english: You should be wary of links sent by strangers.

examples.hanzi: 他的警惕性很高，一有动静就醒了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jǐngtìxìng hěn gāo, yī yǒu dòngjìng jiù xǐng le.
examples.english: He is very alert and wakes at the slightest noise.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.hanzi: 希腊神话里有很多关于英雄和怪兽的故事。
example.pinyin: Xīlà shénhuà lǐ yǒu hěn duō guānyú yīngxióng hé guàishòu de gùshì.
example.english: Greek mythology has many stories about heroes and monsters.
example.fact: The myth of the Kraken, a giant sea monster said to attack ships in Norwegian folklore, likely originated from real but rare sightings of giant squid, which can grow to over 12 meters long and were not scientifically confirmed alive in their natural habitat until a specimen was photographed in 2004.

examples.hanzi: 小时候我最爱听中国神话故事。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoshíhou wǒ zuì ài tīng Zhōngguó shénhuà gùshi.
examples.english: As a child I loved listening to Chinese myths.

examples.hanzi: 这个所谓的完美方案不过是个神话。
examples.pinyin: Zhège suǒwèi de wánměi fāng'àn bùguò shì gè shénhuà.
examples.english: This so-called perfect plan is nothing but a myth.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: an order is spoken.
令 (lìng, order) is a close sound clue for mìng; 令 also in 领 lǐng, 冷 lěng and 零 líng.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 射箭选手一箭命中了靶心。
example.pinyin: shèjiàn xuǎnshǒu yī jiàn mìngzhòng le bǎxīn.
example.english: The archer hit the bullseye with a single arrow.
example.fact: Competitive Olympic archers shoot at a target 70 meters away with a bullseye just 12.2 centimeters wide — roughly the size of a compact disc — and top athletes routinely hit it, a level of precision made possible partly by compound bows with sighting systems that correct for gravity and wind drift.

examples.hanzi: 他投的篮球连续三次命中。
examples.pinyin: Tā tóu de lánqiú liánxù sān cì mìngzhòng.
examples.english: His basketball shots hit the target three times in a row.

examples.hanzi: 这颗子弹没有命中目标。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kē zǐdàn méiyǒu mìngzhòng mùbiāo.
examples.english: The bullet did not hit its target.

components.note: 日 (sun) — summer heat; also in 明 bright, 晴 sunny.
者 (zhě) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 署 shǔ and 薯 shǔ, which sound the same as 暑.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 假 is to borrow or fake, a person lending a false front.
叚 (jiǎ) sounds like 假; also in 暇 xiá and 霞 xiá.

example.hanzi: 暑假期间他去外婆家住了一个月。
example.pinyin: shǔjià qījiān tā qù wàipó jiā zhù le yī gè yuè.
example.english: During summer vacation, he went to stay at his grandmother's house for a month.
example.fact: The long summer break in many school calendars is often traced to the 19th-century agrarian school year, when families needed children free to help with the summer harvest — even though most students today have no farm work waiting for them, the extended summer vacation has largely persisted out of tradition.

examples.hanzi: 你暑假有什么计划吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shǔjià yǒu shénme jìhuà ma?
examples.english: Do you have any plans for the summer vacation?

examples.hanzi: 暑假作业我还没写完呢。
examples.pinyin: Shǔjià zuòyè wǒ hái méi xiě wán ne.
examples.english: I haven't finished my summer homework yet.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks earth and ground, as in 地, 城, 墙; 堡 is an earthen fort.
保 (bǎo) gives the sound exactly: 堡 bǎo.

example.hanzi: 山上有一座古老的城堡。
example.pinyin: Shān shang yǒu yí zuò gǔlǎo de chéngbǎo.
example.english: There is an ancient castle on the mountain.
example.fact: 堡 appears in 城堡 (castle), 堡垒 (stronghold) and 汉堡 (hamburger). In some northern place names it is read bǔ or pù.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在沙滩上堆了一个沙堡。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài shātān shàng duī le yí ge shābǎo.
examples.english: The kids built a sandcastle on the beach.

examples.hanzi: 午饭我想吃汉堡。
examples.pinyin: Wǔfàn wǒ xiǎng chī hànbǎo.
examples.english: I would like a hamburger for lunch.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — striking or acting on something: 放, 改, 政, 教; in 败 a blow breaking a cowry 贝 shell (valuable): ruin, defeat.
贝 (bèi) is a loose sound hint for bài.

example.hanzi: 我们队以一分之差败给了对手。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen duì yǐ yì fēn zhī chā bài gěi le duìshǒu.
example.english: Our team lost to the opponent by one point.
example.fact: 败 pairs with 胜 (win): 胜败. 打败 means to beat, 失败 means to fail. 败家 means to squander the family fortune, and 败家子 is a spendthrift.

examples.hanzi: 这次比赛我们败了，但是不会气馁。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài wǒmen bài le, dànshì bú huì qìněi.
examples.english: We lost this match, but we will not be discouraged.

examples.hanzi: 失败是成功之母。
examples.pinyin: Shībài shì chénggōng zhī mǔ.
examples.english: Failure is the mother of success.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — a hand holding two stalks 禾禾: taking both at once, as in 兼职 side job and 兼顾 look after both.

example.hanzi: 他兼任两个职务。
example.pinyin: Tā jiānrèn liǎng gè zhíwù.
example.english: He holds two posts at once.
example.fact: 兼 means doing two things at once: 兼职 (part-time job), 兼顾 (to look after both), 兼容 (compatible), 兼职 on a CV. It is a formal word.

examples.hanzi: 她白天上班，晚上兼职做家教。
examples.pinyin: Tā báitiān shàngbān, wǎnshang jiānzhí zuò jiājiào.
examples.english: She works in the daytime and tutors part-time in the evening.

examples.hanzi: 这个房间兼作书房和卧室。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān jiānzuò shūfáng hé wòshì.
examples.english: This room serves as both study and bedroom.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees, as in 树, 林; 桃 is the peach tree.
兆 (zhào) — loose sound hint (táo vs zhào); same part in 跳 tiào, 挑 tiāo and 逃 táo.

example.hanzi: 我最喜欢吃桃子。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan chī táozi.
example.english: I love eating peaches the most.
example.fact: The peach is a symbol of longevity: 寿桃 are peach-shaped buns for birthdays. 桃花运 means romantic luck, and 桃花源 is a famous utopia from Tao Yuanming.

examples.hanzi: 院子里有一棵桃树。
examples.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ yǒu yì kē táoshù.
examples.english: There is a peach tree in the yard.

examples.hanzi: 春天桃花开得特别美。
examples.pinyin: Chūntiān táohuā kāi de tèbié měi.
examples.english: In spring the peach blossoms are especially pretty.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 供 is to supply or offer.
共 (gòng) sounds the same except tone; also in 恭 gōng and 洪 hóng.
广 (building, shelter) — the roof-and-wall frame, as in 店, 床, 度. Here it is mostly the outline of the old 應.
心 (heart) — hidden in the traditional 應, 'respond from the heart'; simplification dropped it. 应 is yīng (should) or yìng (respond).

example.hanzi: 这家工厂负责向全市医院供应医疗物资。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngchǎng fùzé xiàng quánshì yīyuàn gōngyìng yīliáo wùzī.
example.english: This factory is responsible for supplying medical materials to hospitals across the city.
example.fact: During the Berlin Airlift of 1948-1949, Allied pilots flew over 200,000 flights in under a year to supply West Berlin with food, coal, and other necessities after Soviet forces blockaded all land routes into the city — at its peak, a cargo plane landed roughly every 45 seconds.

examples.hanzi: 超市每天都会供应新鲜的蔬菜。
examples.pinyin: Chāoshì měitiān dōu huì gōngyìng xīnxiān de shūcài.
examples.english: The supermarket supplies fresh vegetables every day.

examples.hanzi: 这家酒店二十四小时供应热水。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn èrshísì xiǎoshí gōngyìng rèshuǐ.
examples.english: This hotel provides hot water twenty-four hours a day.

components.note: 大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 古人常说"天下大事，分久必合"。
example.pinyin: gǔrén cháng shuō "tiānxià dàshì, fēn jiǔ bì hé".
example.english: The ancients often said, "In the great affairs of the world, long division must eventually reunite."
example.fact: The opening line of the classic Chinese novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms — describing the world's cycles of unity and division — has been quoted so often in Chinese political commentary that it is still regularly invoked today when discussing modern geopolitical shifts, some 600 years after the novel was written.

examples.hanzi: 天下没有免费的午餐。
examples.pinyin: Tiānxià méiyǒu miǎnfèi de wǔcān.
examples.english: There's no such thing as a free lunch in this world.

examples.hanzi: 他的名声传遍了天下。
examples.pinyin: Tā de míngshēng chuánbiàn le tiānxià.
examples.english: His fame spread throughout the land.

components.note: 斗 (dipper, measure) — measuring grain and liquids: 科, 斜, 升; 料 is rice 米 measured out, then material.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 没人料到这场雨会下得这么大。
example.pinyin: méi rén liàodào zhè chǎng yǔ huì xià de zhème dà.
example.english: No one foresaw that this rain would be so heavy.
example.fact: Modern weather forecasting still cannot reliably predict rainfall amounts for a specific location more than about 7 to 10 days in advance, largely because the atmosphere is a chaotic system — a principle famously illustrated by meteorologist Edward Lorenz's 'butterfly effect,' discovered while running weather simulations in the 1960s.

examples.hanzi: 我没料到你会来参加聚会。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méi liàodào nǐ huì lái cānjiā jùhuì.
examples.english: I didn't expect you to come to the party.

examples.hanzi: 谁能料到事情会变成这样？
examples.pinyin: Shéi néng liàodào shìqing huì biànchéng zhèyàng?
examples.english: Who could have predicted things would turn out like this?

components.note: 亻 (person) — urging someone; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
崔 (cuī) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 摧 cuī.
目 (eye) — eyes and seeing, as in 看 look, 睡 sleep, 眼 eye; sleep is closing the eyes.
民 (mín) gives a close sound for mián.

example.hanzi: 心理医生用催眠的方法帮助他戒烟。
example.pinyin: xīnlǐ yīshēng yòng cuīmián de fāngfǎ bāngzhù tā jiè yān.
example.english: The psychologist used hypnosis to help him quit smoking.
example.fact: Modern clinical hypnosis is recognized by the American Psychological Association as a legitimate therapeutic tool, distinct from the stage hypnosis popularized by entertainers — brain imaging studies have shown that hypnotic suggestion can measurably alter activity in regions of the brain involved in pain perception and attention.

examples.hanzi: 这首轻柔的音乐有催眠的效果。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu qīngróu de yīnyuè yǒu cuīmián de xiàoguǒ.
examples.english: This gentle music has a sleep-inducing effect.

examples.hanzi: 老师讲得太无聊，简直像在催眠我们。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī jiǎng de tài wúliáo, jiǎnzhí xiàng zài cuīmián wǒmen.
examples.english: The teacher is so boring it's practically lulling us to sleep.

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.hanzi: 包裹当天就送到了，速度真快。
example.pinyin: bāoguǒ dāngtiān jiù sòngdào le, sùdù zhēn kuài.
example.english: The package arrived on that very day — that's really fast.
example.fact: Same-day delivery services trace back further than e-commerce might suggest — department stores in cities like New York and London were offering same-day horse-drawn cart delivery for local purchases as early as the late 19th century, decades before trucks or airplanes existed.

examples.hanzi: 这张票只在当天有效。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng piào zhǐ zài dāngtiān yǒuxiào.
examples.english: This ticket is only valid on the day of issue.

examples.hanzi: 他当天晚上就坐飞机回国了。
examples.pinyin: Tā dāngtiān wǎnshang jiù zuò fēijī huíguó le.
examples.english: He flew back to his home country that very evening.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 腿 leg, 脸 face.
却 (què) is only a loose sound clue for jiǎo.
足 (foot, ⻊) — foot words, as in 跑 run, 跳 jump.
止 (zhǐ) gives the exact sound; it is also an old picture of a foot, and also sounds out 址 zhǐ.

example.hanzi: 他不小心踢到桌角，脚趾疼了好几天。
example.pinyin: tā bù xiǎoxīn tī dào zhuōjiǎo, jiǎozhǐ téng le hǎojǐ tiān.
example.english: He accidentally kicked the corner of the table, and his toe hurt for several days.
example.fact: Unlike most mammals, humans evolved a relatively short, non-opposable big toe aligned with the other toes, thought to have developed specifically to improve the efficiency of upright walking and running — a trade-off, since it cost our ancestors the ability to grasp branches with their feet the way other apes still can.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝的脚趾又小又可爱。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao de jiǎozhǐ yòu xiǎo yòu kě'ài.
examples.english: The baby's toes are tiny and cute.

examples.hanzi: 这双鞋太小了，挤得我的脚趾很疼。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié tài xiǎo le, jǐ de wǒ de jiǎozhǐ hěn téng.
examples.english: These shoes are too small and squeeze my toes painfully.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — ear radical, as in 聪 clever, 聋 deaf; 耽 first meant drooping ears.
冘 (yín) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 枕 zhěn and 沉 chén.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words and talk: 说, 话, 读; a spoken mistake or misunderstanding.
吴 (wú) gives the sound (wù, tone differs); same series 娱 yú and 虞 yú.

example.hanzi: 长时间的堵车耽误了他的会议。
example.pinyin: Cháng shíjiān de dǔchē dānwu le tā de huìyì.
example.english: The long traffic jam delayed his meeting.
example.fact: Boston's "Big Dig" highway tunnel project took over fifteen years to complete and cost about $14.6 billion, wildly overrunning its original schedule and budget.

examples.hanzi: 对不起，耽误你一点时间。
examples.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, dānwu nǐ yīdiǎn shíjiān.
examples.english: Sorry to take up a bit of your time.

examples.hanzi: 别为了玩游戏耽误了学习。
examples.pinyin: Bié wèile wán yóuxì dānwu le xuéxí.
examples.english: Don't let playing games hold back your studies.

components.note: 米 (rice) — refined grain gives the idea of essence and the best part, hence 精 fine, spirit (精神).
青 (qīng) is a near sound match (-ing); the series 青 清 请 情 晴 静 helps recall jīng.
石 (stone) — stone and hardness, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 码 code: 确 is solid, certain.
角 (jiǎo) replaces 隺 (hè) of 確 and is only a loose clue for què.

example.hanzi: 科学家用精确的仪器测量了地球的周长。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā yòng jīngquè de yíqì cèliáng le dìqiú de zhōucháng.
example.english: Scientists used precise instruments to measure the Earth's circumference.
example.fact: Around 240 BC, the Greek scholar Eratosthenes calculated Earth's circumference using only shadow lengths and simple geometry, landing within about 2% of the modern measured value.

examples.hanzi: 请告诉我精确的时间和地点。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ jīngquè de shíjiān hé dìdiǎn.
examples.english: Please tell me the exact time and place.

examples.hanzi: 他的计算非常精确，一点错误也没有。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jìsuàn fēicháng jīngquè, yīdiǎn cuòwù yě méiyǒu.
examples.english: His calculation is very precise, without a single error.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 流 is flowing water.
㐬 (liú) — same sound — 流 is liú; 㐬 also sounds out 琉 liú and 硫 liú.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and waves: 河, 海, 汤; 浪 is a wave.
良 (liáng) is a loose clue; also in 狼 láng, 朗 lǎng and 娘 niáng.
氵 (water) — marks rivers and water, as in 河, 海, 江; 汉 is the Han River, which gave name to the Han dynasty and people.

example.hanzi: 那个流浪汉每天坐在公园的长椅上。
example.pinyin: Nàge liúlànghàn měitiān zuò zài gōngyuán de chángyǐ shàng.
example.english: That wanderer sits on the park bench every day.
example.fact: The ancient Greek philosopher Diogenes of Sinope reportedly lived by choice in a large ceramic jar in the Athens marketplace, rejecting material possessions as part of his Cynic philosophy.

examples.hanzi: 天太冷了，流浪汉睡在地铁站里。
examples.pinyin: Tiān tài lěng le, liúlànghàn shuì zài dìtiězhàn lǐ.
examples.english: It was so cold that the homeless man slept in the subway station.

examples.hanzi: 我给那个流浪汉买了一份热饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nàge liúlànghàn mǎi le yī fèn rè fàn.
examples.english: I bought a hot meal for that homeless man.
